learning.title: Configure Inngest through env vars and bind with the bracketed IPv6 wildcard
learning.trigger: Starting inngest start in a container where secrets must stay off the command line or the private network may be IPv6.
learning.rule: Inngest v1.44.0 honours its flags as INNGEST_* environment variables: INNGEST_HOST, INNGEST_PORT, INNGEST_POSTGRES_URI, INNGEST_REDIS_URI, INNGEST_EVENT_KEY, INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY, INNGEST_SDK_URL, INNGEST_POLL_INTERVAL, INNGEST_TICK, INNGEST_POSTGRES_MAX_OPEN_CONNS and INNGEST_POSTGRES_MAX_IDLE_CONNS. Pass URIs and keys that way so nothing secret appears in /proc/PID/cmdline. A missing event or signing key name silently falls back to dev defaults, so prove each name.

Bind with INNGEST_HOST=[::]. A bare :: fails with listen tcp: address :::PORT: too many colons in address. [::] listens on the tcp6 wildcard, dual-stack with Linux bindv6only=0, so one bind serves Railway's A and AAAA private addresses.

verification.requirement: The container image has no pgrep or ps; read /proc/PID/cmdline and /proc/net/tcp6 to prove no secret on argv and a wildcard LISTEN.
Prove the event key (configured key accepted, wrong key refused), signing key and SDK URL (app synced), and Redis URI (state keys present in Redis).

learning.boundary: The local proof network was IPv4 only; IPv6 reachability itself was not exercised, only the tcp6 wildcard bind. The /proc probes ran inside the committed proof script infra/railway/local-proof/prove.sh. An inline docker exec sh -c loop was refused by the Claude Code safety check and was not retried in another form.
